newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes higher in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes higher in moderate trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed initial weakness to end firmer against its American counterpart on Friday, spurred by late U.S. dollar selling, dealers said.
The local unit was weak for most of the day but late selling on the U.S. dollar pulled the rate to end at T$27.487 against Thursday's T$27.492 close.
Turnover through dealers was a moderate US$187 million.
Some local banks started to sell U.S. dollars in Taiwan's late afternoon, reflecting the dollar's fall against the yen and other major currencies in the Tokyo afternoon, dealers said.
Jitters about the U.S. dollar were heightened by the approach of the weekend, although Taiwan's foreign exchange market does open on Saturday morning.
"With the weekend coming, investors do not want to hold too many positions when overseas markets are moving so actively," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"It nonetheless will be hard for the Taiwan dollar to breach the T$27.48 level," the dealer said, noting the central bank's long-term policy of maintaining a stable foreign exchange rate.
A T$27.48-50 range was seen in the near term.
